newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to set up US$ bills market by end-1997.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to set up US$ bills market by end-1997.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank and finance ministry said on Saturday they planned to set up a U.S. dollar-denominated bills market by the end of 1997 in a bid to develop Taiwan into a regional financial centre.
The two agencies said in a statement that they planned to allow banks to issue U.S. dollar-denominated negotiable certificates of deposits in June 1997.

The two proposed to allow businesses, based on actual trading needs, to issue U.S. dollar-denominated acceptance bills, the statement said, but they did not give a timetable for the move, saying they will do it in "appropriate time."
The two will open bills finance firms, or money market brokers, to operate U.S. dollar-denominated acceptance bills and negotiable certificates of deposits by the end of 1997, the statement said.
The planned opening of the new business to bills finance firms suggests the central bank and finance ministry will allow businesses to issue U.S. dollar acceptance bills by end-1997.
